It is important to underscore the important principle that is at stake in this case. Respondent argues that "Being a communicant member is a necessary, but not a sufficient condition for voting (BCO 6-4; 25-1)" (emphasis added), and that PCA congregations have

artifacts.synopsis: Mr. Psiaki complained that Covenant Presbyterian Church's Session erred in installing officers elected at a congregational meeting that excluded communicant members under age 18 from voting, in violation of the BCO. The SJC sustained the complaint (15-5), holding that all communicant members have a constitutional right to vote in officer elections regardless of age, and that church bylaws may not override BCO provisions; multiple dissenting opinions argued that BCO 20-3 and 24-3's phrase 'good and regular standing' permits local sessions to establish reasonable minimum voting ages.

artifacts.title: Dailey v. Heritage Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: RE Dailey complained that Heritage Presbytery erred in upholding its Moderator's ruling that a church member's document was administratively in order as a complaint under BCO 43-3, after the Session had ruled it out of order. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that neither triggering condition of BCO 43-3 was met because the Session's ruling that the document did not qualify as a BCO 43-1 complaint was not equivalent to denying it, and the Session had considered and responded to the matter in a timely manner. A substantial dissent argued for a broader interpretation of 'fails to consider' in BCO 43-3.
